title: UPAC Work in Progress: Dark Energy & the Spacetime-Matter Dichotomy
speaker: Niels Martens (Utrecht University)
description: UPAC Colloquium (Utrecht Philosophy of Astronomy & Cosmology): work-in-progress session; the draft is sent out beforehand via the upac-l mailing list. Hybrid; the Teams link goes out via the same list.
abstract: This chapter concerns the cosmological constant as a case study for a critical assessment of the conceptual dichotomy between spacetime and matter. The explanation of the accelerated expansion of our universe by the cosmological constant proceeds via the Raychaudhuri equation, after imposing an energy condition, either in its matter or spacetime form. As there seems to be no objective preference for the spacetime-like or matterlike explanation, the cosmological constant does not neatly fit the mold of the spacetime-matter dichotomy, at least not explanatorily speaking. Along the way I critically discuss Baker's (2005) argument for substantivalism from the cosmological constant, and reflect on the various uses of the energy conditions and energy criteria.
